lessons.title: Lesson 1: Picking the right free tool for the job
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 4 minutes
Goal: Match an everyday task to the free AI tool that fits it.
This lesson builds toward: Given an everyday task, you will choose the free tool that fits it: a chat assistant, a translation app or a design tool, matching at least 4 of 5 tasks to the right kind of tool.
Think of AI tools like tools in a kitchen drawer. Each one is good at a different job.
An AI chat assistant (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot or Google Gemini) is good for writing, explaining and planning. A translation app (like Google Translate) is good for other languages. A design tool (like Canva, which has a free version) is good for flyers and cards.
Start with the task, not the tool. Ask yourself: do I need words written, words translated, or something that looks nice to print or share?
Step by step:
- Write down the task you need to do.
- Decide: do you need words written, translated, or designed?
- Pick the tool that matches: chat assistant, translation app or design tool.
- Use the free version first.
Words to know:
- Chat assistant: an AI program you write or talk to, which writes answers back.
- Free version: the no-cost level of a tool; some tools also sell extra features.
Try it now: List three tasks you have this month. Next to each, write which kind of tool fits: chat assistant, translation app or design tool.
You can now match an everyday task to the right free AI tool.

check.q: Which kind of tool is best for putting a letter into another language?
check.why: A translation app is made for changing words into another language.

check.q: You need a thank-you card for volunteers that looks nice to print. What do you open first?
check.why: A design tool is made for cards and flyers that look nice to print or share.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Talking to AI with your voice
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Ask an AI assistant a question by speaking instead of typing.
This lesson builds toward: Using a phone or an AI assistant app, you will ask a question by speaking and fix any words the voice typing got wrong, before you send it.
If typing is slow or hard for you, you can talk instead. Most AI assistant apps have a microphone button. Tap it, speak your question, and the app turns your words into text.
Phones also have voice typing built into the keyboard. Look for a small microphone on the keyboard when you are typing a message.
Speak clearly and a little slower than normal. Say what you need, like: "Help me write a short note to my son's teacher saying he will miss school on Friday for a doctor visit." Read the words before you send them, because voice typing can mishear.
Step by step:
- Open the AI assistant app or a message on your phone.
- Find the microphone button.
- Tap it and speak your question clearly.
- Read the words it heard, fix any mistakes, then send.
Words to know:
- Voice typing: a phone feature that turns what you say into written words.
- Microphone button: a small button with a microphone picture that lets the device listen.
Try it now: Use the microphone button to ask an AI assistant to write a two-sentence note to a teacher, boss or neighbor. Read it and fix any mistakes.
You can now ask an AI assistant for help using your voice and check what it heard.

check.q: Where do you often find voice typing on a phone?
options: A small microphone on the keyboard
check.why: Phone keyboards often have a small microphone button for voice typing.

check.q: You spoke a note and the app wrote "by bread" instead of "buy bread". What do you do?
options: Fix the words before you send
check.why: Voice typing can mishear, so you read and fix the words before sending.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Translating with your phone camera
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Translate a printed sign, label or letter by pointing your phone camera at it.
This lesson builds toward: Given a printed sign, label or notice in another language, you will translate it with a phone camera and decide when to ask for an interpreter or a fluent reader, using an interpreter for medical or legal papers.
Free apps like Google Translate can read printed words through your phone camera and show them in another language. This helps with signs, medicine labels, school notices and forms written in a language you do not read well.
In the app, pick the two languages (the one on the paper and the one you want), choose the camera option, and point your phone at the words.
Machine translation is helpful but not perfect. For medicine, legal papers or anything important, ask for an interpreter. Many hospitals, clinics and government offices offer one at no cost; ask at the front desk.
Step by step:
- Install a free translation app from the official app store.
- Pick the language on the paper and the language you want.
- Choose the camera option and point your phone at the words.
- For important papers, ask the office for an interpreter.
Words to know:
- Translate: to change words from one language into another.
- Interpreter: a trained person who translates speech between two languages.
Try it now: Point a translation app's camera at a printed label or sign in your home (a food box works). Translate it into another language and back.
You can now translate printed words with your phone camera, and know when to ask for a person instead.

check.q: What is true about machine translation?
options: It is helpful but not perfect
check.why: Free translation is a strong help but can make mistakes.

check.q: Your medicine label is in a language you do not read well. What is the safest step?
options: Ask the pharmacy or clinic for an interpreter
check.why: For medicine and legal papers, a trained interpreter is the safest help.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Writing short messages with an AI assistant
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 4 minutes
Goal: Get an AI assistant to write a short, clear message in the tone you want.
This lesson builds toward: Given a message you need to send, you will ask an AI assistant for a short message with the reader, content, tone and length, then edit it and check every fact, so it sounds like you and every date and place is right.
An AI assistant can write short messages for you: a reminder to your community group, a note to a landlord, or a thank-you to a volunteer.
Tell it who the message is for, what it must say, and the tone: friendly, polite, or firm. Tell it how long: "three sentences" or "under 50 words".
Then make it yours. Change words that do not sound like you, and check names, dates and places yourself.
Step by step:
- Say who the message is for.
- Say what it must include: date, time, place, what to bring.
- Say the tone and the length.
- Edit it so it sounds like you, and check every fact.
Words to know:
- Tone: how a message sounds: friendly, polite, serious or firm.
Try it now: Ask an AI assistant: "Write a friendly three-sentence reminder for my neighbors about a block clean-up on Saturday at 9 am. Bring gloves." Then change one line so it sounds like you.
You can now get an AI assistant to write a short message with the right tone and length, then make it your own.

check.q: What does "tone" mean in a message?
options: How it sounds, like friendly or firm
check.why: Tone is how a message sounds to the reader.

check.q: The AI's reminder says the clean-up is Sunday, but it is Saturday. What do you do?
options: Send it; the AI knows best
Ask everyone to come both days
Change it to Saturday before sending
check.why: You check every fact yourself and fix it before you send.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Designing a simple flyer with Canva
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Make a one-page flyer in the free version of Canva.
This lesson builds toward: Using the free version of Canva, you will create a one-page flyer from a template with a title, what, when and where, and one picture, downloaded or shared, and signed out on a shared computer.
Canva is a design website and app with a free version. It has ready-made templates, so you do not need to be an artist. You can use it at canva.com on a library computer or in its app on your phone.
Search Canva for a template, such as "flyer" or "event flyer". Click one you like, then click on its words to replace them with yours. Keep it simple: a big title, three short lines (what, when, where), and one picture.
When you finish, download it to print, or share it by text or email. Canva asks you to make a free account; on a shared computer, sign out when you finish.
Step by step:
- Go to canva.com or open the Canva app and sign up for a free account.
- Search for a flyer template and pick one.
- Click each piece of text and type your own words.
- Keep it to a title, three short lines and one picture.
- Download or share it, then sign out on a shared computer.
Words to know:
- Template: a ready-made design you fill in with your own words and pictures.
- Download: to save a copy of a file onto your device.
Try it now: Open Canva, pick a flyer template, and replace the words with the reminder you wrote in Lesson 4. Download it or save it to your account.
You can now make a simple, clear flyer using a free Canva template.

check.q: What is a template in Canva?
options: A ready-made design you fill in with your words
check.why: A template is a ready-made design, so you only change the words and pictures.

check.q: Your flyer has eight lines of small text. How do you make it easier to read?
options: Cut it to a title and three short lines
check.why: A big title and three short lines (what, when, where) are easiest to read.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Putting the tools together
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use a chat assistant, a design tool and a translation tool together to make one finished flyer in two languages.
This lesson builds toward: Using the free version of Canva, you will create a one-page flyer from a template with a title, what, when and where, and one picture, downloaded or shared, and signed out on a shared computer. Given a printed sign, label or notice in another language, you will translate it with a phone camera and decide when to ask for an interpreter or a fluent reader, using an interpreter for medical or legal papers.
Real projects often use more than one tool. For a community flyer, you can use the chat assistant to write the words, Canva to design it, and a translation tool to make a second version.
Ask the AI for a short title and three lines of details. Paste them into a Canva template. Then translate the same words into a second language your neighbors speak and make a copy of the flyer with them.
Ask someone who speaks that language to read the translation if you can. Free tools are a strong start; a real reader makes it right.
Step by step:
- Ask a chat assistant for a title and three lines of details.
- Put the words into a Canva flyer template.
- Translate the words into a second language.
- Make a copy of the flyer with the translation.
- Ask a fluent speaker to read it if you can.
Words to know:
- Project: a piece of work with a clear finished result, like a flyer.
Try it now: Final task: make a one-page flyer for a community event. Use an AI assistant to write a title and three lines, design it in Canva, and make a second copy translated into another language your neighbors speak.
You can now use several free AI tools together to finish a real project for your community.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Words from the assistant No title or details, or the words were not checked. A short title and three lines from the AI, edited to sound right, with dates and places checked. Asked the AI for a change, such as a friendlier tone or a shorter title. Flyer design No flyer, or it is crowded and hard to read. A one-page Canva flyer with a big title, what, when and where, and one picture. Downloaded or shared it, and it reads clearly from across a room. Second language No translated copy. A second copy with the words translated into a language neighbors speak. A fluent speaker read the translation and it was fixed if needed. Right tool for each step Cannot say which tool did which job. Names the chat assistant, Canva and the translation tool for each step. Explains why each tool fits its job. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.q: In the combined project, what do you paste into the Canva template?
options: The title and three lines the AI wrote
A link to the AI website
check.why: The chat assistant writes the words, and you put them into the Canva flyer.

check.q: You translated your flyer into Spanish but do not speak Spanish. What do you do before sharing?
options: Ask a fluent Spanish speaker to read it
check.why: A real reader catches mistakes the free tool missed.
